propositions: A ticket description edit verified at 14,997 chars was silently reverted to a 10,582 char older revision without error or ConcurrencyError, causing data loss and corruption of acceptance criteria.

Optimistic concurrency protection failed to reject a write that was reported successful, verified by read-back, and then rolled back — violating the documented guarantee that conflicting writes raise ConcurrencyError.
A ticket description edit occurred while the same ticket's plan-review was in flight emitting REVIEW_RESULT sidecar events, and store reconvergence between the two writers is suspected as the cause.
Read-back verification is insufficient to prevent silent data loss, invalidating the documented mitigation of reading back after writes to confirm success.
A newer EDIT event carrying stale client-held description text can silently overwrite fresher content via last-writer-wins reduction without explicit compare-and-swap or base revision fingerprinting.

A fixed reducer cache race (commit 0b964c82f5) that allowed stale cached state to be published alongside current event hashes previously explained the behavior but does not fully exclude stale whole-field overwrites under concurrent conditions.
